facts.statement: Eskimaspis is an extinct genus of arthrodire placoderm fish that lived during the Early Devonian period.
facts.quote: Eskimaspis is an extinct monospecific genus of arthrodire placoderm fish from the Early Devonian period.

facts.statement: The type species Eskimaspis heintzi was described in 1984 from fossils found in the Peel Sound Formation on Prince of Wales Island in Arctic Canada.
facts.quote: The type species Eskimaspis heintzi was described in 1984, and was found in the Peel Sound Formation on Prince of Wales Island in Arctic Canada.

facts.statement: The genus name Eskimaspis honors the aboriginal Eskimo people of the Canadian Arctic.
facts.quote: The generic name Eskimaspis was named after the aboriginal Eskimo people of the Canadian Arctic.

facts.statement: Eskimaspis is considered one of the most basal members of the order Arthrodira.

facts.statement: Eskimaspis belongs to the class Placodermi and the parent group Arthrodira.
Eskimaspis lived during the Lochkovian stage, approximately 419.62 to 413.02 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Lochkovian to Lochkovian (419.62 to 413.02 million years ago)
